names.official: Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China

summary: Hong Kong's Immigration Department publishes its own visa requirements: around 150 nationalities visit visa-free for between 7 and 180 days depending on passport, Indian nationals complete a free online pre-arrival registration, and a minority of passports need an entry visa before travel.

notes: Hong Kong Customs allows passengers aged 18 or over to bring in duty-free, for their own use, only 1 litre of alcoholic liquor above 30% and 19 cigarettes (or 1 cigar, 25 g of cigars or 25 g of other tobacco).
The UK FCDO says it is prohibited to bring e-cigarettes, heated tobacco products, herbal cigarettes or related devices into Hong Kong, including in personal luggage.

payments.text: No official source we read describes card acceptance in Hong Kong. The currency is the Hong Kong dollar (HKD), according to the Government of Canada.

safety.text: The UK Foreign Office says violent crime is low but pickpocketing and other street crime can happen, that the typhoon season runs from May to November, and that national security laws can be interpreted broadly. It says protests are rare but could take place at any time, and that if you are near a demonstration you should follow the advice of local authorities and move away.

tips.text: The Government of Canada says that if you plan to visit or transit through mainland China you should obtain a Chinese visa before your trip, and that travel between Hong Kong, Macao and mainland China needs a visa allowing multiple entries.

Indian nationals must complete the free online Pre-arrival Registration before they can visit Hong Kong visa-free. A registration is valid for six months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days each.

The UK FCDO says the typhoon season runs from May to November, that public offices and public transport shut down when a Typhoon 8 signal is raised, and that you should follow local warnings and check the Hong Kong Observatory.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: Probably not: around 150 nationalities enter visa-free, from 7 days up to 180 days depending on passport — 90 days for the EU, US, Canada, Australia, Japan and most major passports, and 180 days for British citizens. Indian nationals pre-register online for free; a minority of nationalities need an advance entry visa from the Immigration Department.

faq.question: Is a Chinese visa valid for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: No official source we could read says a mainland Chinese visa is valid for Hong Kong: Hong Kong's Immigration Department publishes its own visa requirements, under which most nationalities visit visa-free. The Government of Canada says that if you plan to visit or transit through mainland China you should obtain a Chinese visa before your trip.

faq.question: How long can British citizens stay in Hong Kong?
faq.answer: British citizens can visit visa-free for up to 180 days — the most generous tier of Hong Kong's visa-waiver arrangements.

faq.question: Do Indian citizens need a visa for Hong Kong?
faq.answer: Not a visa, but a Pre-arrival Registration (PAR) — a free online registration with the Immigration Department completed before travel. It is valid for 6 months and allows multiple visits of up to 14 days each; airlines check it at boarding.

faq.question: Can I extend my stay in Hong Kong as a visitor?
faq.answer: Extension of limit of stay is applied for at the Immigration Department; its fee table lists HK$330 for a change of condition of stay, including an extension of limit of stay. The Department says that, except in the most unusual circumstances, visitors are not allowed to change their immigration status after arrival. No official source we could read states when a visitor's extension is granted.
